why: Keep the newest recovery snapshot and avoid redundant checkpoint writes when several saves queue across independent copying.
verdict: pass for six controlled native ordering cases plus frozen browser regression
reproducedFailure: After two queued post-copy checkpoints completed, saving the exact latest snapshot performed another write because copy completion had reset the request marker to its older captured snapshot.
fix: Copy completion preserves a newer queued save request marker.
Recovery migration is shared between copy completion and changed-identity queued writes, so a temporary transfer quota failure can retry before saving.
verified: Original four preceding-save/conflict and later-success/failure cases
Two queued post-copy checkpoints retain the newest snapshot while the first write is held
Successful transfer and temporary recovery-storage-full transfer retry
Latest committed snapshot save coalesces without another write
Real public frozen-release two-tab conflict/copy quota retry and exact pre-first-frame reload
limits: Controlled recovery quota fails once; sustained unavailable storage remains outside this result.
No process-termination at every microtask boundary or all simultaneous restart combinations.
